title: Break-even Scenarios by Model & Region (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet explores break-even per-request/token prices across model families and regions under multiple supply/traffic scenarios. Goal is to produce actionable levers (batching, cache, routing, quantization) and a short prioritized rollout for Hosted API to protect margin targets when running different model mixes.

High level assumptions (editable):
- Time horizon: 12 month rolling (base month = Oct 2025).
- Capacity types: reserved-dedicated (committed), on-demand (cloud/GPU hourly), spot/ephemeral pricing buckets.
- Models included: rwd-7B, rwd-30B, rwd-70B, open-13B, open-70B (representative families).
- Average tokens per request (APTR): chat assistant = 450 tokens, embeddings = 64 tokens, rerank = 1,200 tokens (avg).
- Customer traffic buckets: PLG-async (latency tolerant), Enterprise-sync (low latency).
- Exchange rate layer: USD baseline; FX scenarios: +10%/-10% vendor cloud costs.

Tabs (sheet structure):
1) Assumptions - editable knobs (APTR by workload, GPU $/hour by region/type, reserved discount %, on-demand premium, slot efficiency)
2) Per-model throughput - tokens/sec per GPU, batch size sensitivity table (batch 1, 4, 16, 64)
3) Regional COGS - breakdown by compute, storage/cache, egress, infra overhead, amortized infra licensing (per-token basis)
4) Breakeven Matrix - model x region x traffic-scenario -> required price per 1k tokens to hit target margin
5) Levers & Ops - recommended short/medium actions + estimated impact on unit cost
6) Sensitivity - tornado charts for APTR, token throughput, reserved-utilization
7) Notes & open-questions - for follow-up with infra, pricing, sales

Representative calculations (examples from Breakeven Matrix):
- rwd-30B, us-west1, baseline traffic (70% reserved util, batch 8 average):
  - compute COGS: $0.028 per 1k tokens
  - infra & overhead: $0.004 per 1k tokens
  - storage/kv cache amortized: $0.002 per 1k tokens (assuming 12% cache hit -> reduces compute by effective 8%)
  - total COGS: $0.034 per 1k tokens -> breakeven price to hit 30% gross margin = $0.048 per 1k tokens

- open-70B, eu-west1, low reserved util (30%), no batching (latency-critical):
  - compute COGS: $0.26 per 1k tokens
  - infra & overhead: $0.012 per 1k tokens
  - caching benefit negligible (workload not cacheable)
  - total COGS: $0.272 per 1k tokens -> breakeven at 30% margin = $0.389 per 1k tokens

Key sensitivity observations (quick notes):
- Reserved utilization is the single biggest lever for hosted API unit econ for large models: moving reserved util from 30% to 70% reduces per-token compute cost by ~40–55% for rwd-70B/open-70B depending on batch efficiency.
- Batching helps smaller models too: for rwd-7B moving from batch=1 to batch=16 improves tokens/sec by ~3.6x on our runtime; effect on per-token cost ~-65% in compute line.
- KV cache is high ROI for assistant-style workloads with repeated prefixes (dialogue). A conservative 15% cache hit yields ~8–12% per-token savings for large models.
- FX and regional power/instance scarcity create bite-sized pockets where on-demand costs spike (example: ap-southeast unusual spot premiums -> +18% compute COGS).

Scenarios modeled (sheet):
A) Baseline (current mix, reserved util 60%, medium batching)
B) Growth (traffic +2.5x, require 40% on-demand to cover bursts)
C) Enterprise shift (more sync low-latency requests -> batching down, reserved util up due to contracts)
D) Stress (spot market events -> spot unavailable -> on-demand only for 48hrs)

Shortlist of recommended product/ops levers (priority + estimated delta on COGS):
- Auto-batching across PLG pool (alpha): expected -18% compute COGS for typical PLG queries (priority: P0 for Q2 pilot).
- Per-customer model pinning -> allow enterprise customers to request reserved capacity pinning (-guarantees), increases reserved util predictability. (priority: P1)
- Route low-value requests to quantized model variants by default (rwd-7B/q4 -> -28% compute). (priority: P1)
- Aggressive KV cache for assistant templates and session affinity (pilot on high-traffic tenants) -> model dependent -8% to -15% effective token cost. (priority: P0)
- Regional spot hedging: pre-warm cross-region capacity to absorb spot loss windows (ops playbook). (priority: P2)

Open questions / decisions for next meeting:
- Target margin band by customer tier (PLG vs enterprise) — finance to confirm target gross margin thresholds for compute pass-through or bundled pricing.
- How to price on-demand model variant in console to reflect higher COGS without breaking UX. Product needs examples for console text.
- Confirm allowed quantization levels for each model family (research + model-ops).
- SLA implications for aggressive batch windows on enterprise-sync traffic. SRE to evaluate tail latency impact.

Immediate next steps (owners / 2-week sprint):
- [Maya] lock down APTR estimation by workload (collect token histograms from hosted-api logs).
- [Ethan] run synthetic batch throughput benchmarks for rwd-30B & open-70B across eu/us/ap regions and upload CSV into Tab "Per-model throughput".
- [Lina] simulate 48hr stress spot-loss scenario and produce cost delta chart.
- [Samir] draft console copy for "on-demand premium" pricing and coordinate with growth on messaging.

Appendix: quick formulas used in sheet (explicit):
- compute_per_1k = (GPU_hourly_cost / (tokens_per_sec * 3600)) * 1000 * (1 + infra_overhead_pct) * (1 - cache_effective_reduction)
- breakeven_price = compute_per_1k / (1 - target_margin)

Notes on data quality: some cost inputs are coarse (vendor hourly prices pulled from vendor ratecards; spot discounts are historical averages). Action: we should source 90-day rolling hourly price feed for each region to make Stress scenarios defensible.

This is a working draft — please comment inline on the sheet tabs (linked files above) and flag any assumptions that should move to the canonical Playbook.

Document history: created 2025-09-15 by Maya Patel; iterative updates through Feb–Mar 2026 for benchmarking results.

End of draft.
